[{"node": "menu_content107", "element": "menu_content", "data": {"label": "Permissions", "key": "permissions_menu_content", "id": "permissions_menu_content", "name": "permissions_menu_content"}, "elements": [{"node": "markdown101", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "Restaurant roles", "key": "md_restaurant_roles", "id": "restaurant-roles", "name": "md_restaurant_roles", "value": "# Restaurant roles

A **Restaurant Role** is what a person may do in the POS. Server, Bartender, Host, Cashier and Manager come installed; edit them or create your own. Each role turns on or off:

| Permission | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Every table of the restaurant | Work on any table, not only the assigned ones |
| See / work on other people's orders | Open and change orders taken by someone else |
| Transfer, divide | Move orders between tables, split them |
| Maximum discount % | The largest discount without approval |
| Change price | Set a different rate on a line |
| Void sent items, void orders | Remove what the kitchen already has |
| Take payments, cash register | Charge and open / close their register |
| Open the drawer without a sale | Logged every time |
| Reprint, mark 86, reservations | |
| Edit floor plan, edit menu | |
| Approve with PIN | Can authorize others with their PIN |

**Restaurant Manager** and **System Manager** users can do everything.
"}}, {"node": "markdown102", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "Who works where", "key": "md_who_works_where", "id": "who-works-where", "name": "md_who_works_where", "value": "# Who works where

In the **POS Profile**, each person in the user list has a **Restaurant Permission** button. There you set:

- their **role** (if empty, the *Default Role* of Restaurant Settings applies);
- the **floors, rooms, tables and production centers** they work in. A floor includes its rooms, tables and centers; a room includes its tables.

A person can be listed in several POS Profiles of the same restaurant: **what each one grants adds up**. The role comes from the POS Profile in use (their default one).
"}}, {"node": "markdown103", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "My access", "key": "md_my_access", "id": "my-access", "name": "md_my_access", "value": "# My access

Not sure why someone sees (or doesn't see) a table? Log in as that person and open **My access** in the staff menu. It shows:

- the restaurant and the **POS Profile in use**, and why it was chosen;
- the **role** and where it comes from (the POS Profile, the default role, or full access as a manager);
- how many floors, rooms, tables and centers they can see;
- every POS Profile they are listed in, whether it counts, and what it grants.
"}}, {"node": "markdown104", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "Approvals with a manager PIN", "key": "md_approvals_with_a_manager_pin", "id": "approvals-with-a-manager-pin", "name": "md_approvals_with_a_manager_pin", "value": "# Approvals with a manager PIN

When a role doesn't allow something (a 30% discount, voiding a sent item, working on someone else's order), Ren asks right there for the **PIN of someone who may approve it**. The approver sees what they are approving, including the amount.

An approval is valid once, for that action, that order and that amount, for two minutes. Approving work on someone else's order unlocks that order for 30 minutes. Every approval and every rejected PIN is written to the **Restaurant Audit Log**.
"}}, {"node": "markdown105", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "PINs, clock in and shared terminals", "key": "md_pins_clock_in_and_shared_terminals", "id": "pins-clock-in-and-shared-terminals", "name": "md_pins_clock_in_and_shared_terminals", "value": "# PINs, clock in and shared terminals

- Each person sets their own **PIN** (4 to 8 digits) from the staff menu. Managers can reset their staff's PIN.
- **Clock in / out** from the staff menu. Turn on *Staff must clock in to take orders* in Restaurant Settings to make it mandatory.
- A manager can **register a device as a terminal**. On that device, staff switch user at **/pos_login** by tapping their name and typing their PIN. Only the staff of that terminal's POS Profile can log in there (never administrators); five wrong PINs lock that person on that terminal for five minutes.
"}}, {"node": "markdown106", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "Audit log", "key": "md_audit_log", "id": "audit-log", "name": "md_audit_log", "value": "# Audit log

The **Restaurant Audit Log** records approvals, rejected PINs, discounts and price changes, drawer openings, transfers, PIN logins and terminal registrations: who, what, the amount, the order and who approved it.
"}}]}]
